Granite belongs to intrusive rock; it is first formed by underground magma intruding and cooling and crystallizing to form a granite body; afterward, regional crustal uplift raises the position of the rock body that was originally located deep underground; then, after long-term weathering and denudation, the overlying rock layers are removed and the peak-column form is shaped; finally, erosion and transportation carry away the products of weathering and denudation, causing the granite to be further exposed.
